description: A `struct` type name colliding with the keyword `mod` raises `ol-reserved-word` at phase-1 registration, `stage: "runtime"` -- `execute()` runs `parse()` only, never `check()`, so the runtime carries its own declaration-slot guard (`execute-internal.ts`'s `collectStructs`; `spec/data-structures.md:323` gives `struct` the `ol-reserved-word` diagnostic and phase-1 registration, and `:304` states the split this fixture turns on: "Field names are bindings, not declarations, so any name is legal there ... The type name is a declaration: it registers a constructor in the callable namespace, so a built-in name raises `ol-reserved-word`"). This is the RUNTIME axis of issue #837: `mod` joined the keyword registry both sides read, so it collides here exactly as `struct and` already did, with `namespace: "reserved"` rather than `"primitive"` (spec/grammar.md:373,378 -- `and`/`or`/`not`/`mod` are word-spelled operators of the expression grammar, not callable primitives). Note the field list `[ x y ]` is a binding position and stays unrestricted. The check-stage and binding/call axes are pinned by core-language/check/reserved-word-define-mod and keyword-mod-binds-and-calls-freely.

diagnostics.message: mod is already a reserved, so it can't be redefined here.
